records.title: Measure of restricted signed periodic dilations
records.statement: For measurable 1-periodic H of density d, A=σLH has period L and measure Ld on every period. If R=mL+r, 0≤r<L, then m(A∩I)≤mLd+min(r,Ld) for every interval I of length R. In particular m((σ2^kH)∩[0,1])≤max(1,2^k)d, with equality d when k≤0.
hypotheses: H⊂ℝ is Lebesgue measurable and H+1=H.
I is an interval of finite length R≥0.
conclusion: Signed scaling preserves density and rescales the period.
The dyadic restriction bound controls expanding and contracting scales.
proof: Change variables for positive scaling; reflect and use periodicity for negative scaling to obtain measure Ld on [0,L).
Every length-L interval has the same measure: reduce its start modulo L, split at L, and translate the second piece by −L.
Decompose I into m whole periods plus a remainder of length r, whose measure is at most both r and Ld.
If L=2^k≤1, the unit interval contains exactly 2^(−k) periods. If L>1, it is contained in one period.
limitations: Without periodicity, unit-interval measure does not control scaled restrictions.
For k>0 the factor 2^k cannot generally be omitted.

records.title: Summable budgets for signed dyadic scales
records.statement: For r>2, Σ_{k∈ℤ}r^(−|k|)max(1,2^k)=1+1/(r−1)+2/(r−2). At r=4 this is 7/3. If ρ(H_k)≤Cα4^(−|k|), then the union of both signed dyadic dilations has unit-interval measure at most 14Cα/3.
hypotheses: Every H_k is measurable and 1-periodic with density ≤Cα4^(−|k|).
conclusion: For C=6 and α=η/64 this is 7η/16.
proof: Split into negative, zero, and positive k.
Apply countable subadditivity and the restriction lemma to both signs.
limitations: At r≤2 the positive-scale majorant diverges; this does not prove that the actual union has large measure.
The signed sets need not be disjoint.

records.title: Pointwise normalization of all signed nonzero dilations
records.statement: If every H_k hits every y+t a_n with y∈ℝ and t∈[1,2), then U=⋃_{k∈ℤ}(2^kH_k∪−2^kH_k) hits every x+s a_n with x∈ℝ and s≠0.
hypotheses: For every k∈ℤ, every y∈ℝ, and every t∈[1,2), some n≥1 satisfies y+t a_n∈H_k.
proof: Take n with y+t a_n∈H_k. Multiplication by σ2^k gives x+s a_n∈σ2^kH_k⊂U.
limitations: The same index n is used, with no reindexing or relation to the ratio of any geometric sequence.
Pointwise uniform hitting is required for this argument.

records.title: Finite-range obstruction to arbitrarily sparse periodic hitting
records.statement: If finite A⊂ℝ has N distinct elements and measurable 1-periodic H hits x+A for every x∈ℝ, then ρ(H)≥1/N. The identically zero null sequence therefore cannot satisfy arbitrarily-small-density normalized hitting.
hypotheses: A is finite and nonempty with N distinct elements.
conclusion: N can be replaced by the number of distinct residues of A modulo 1.
Convergence a_n→0 alone does not supply normalized hitting sets.
proof: Each H−a has unit-interval measure ρ(H).
Finite subadditivity yields 1≤Nρ(H). Equal residues give identical translated sets.
For A={0}, the condition forces H=ℝ, of density 1.
limitations: This is an obstruction to the hitting hypothesis, not a disproof of a similarity conjecture for infinite sets.

examples.conclusion: Hitting all centers forces H=ℝ, so density ≤Cp fails for p<1/C.

records.title: Normalized periodic hitting implies large compact affine avoidance
records.statement: For any fixed real sequence (a_n), if ∃C∈(0,∞) ∀p∈(0,1) ∃open 1-periodic H_p with ρ(H_p)≤Cp and ∀y∈ℝ ∀t∈[1,2) ∃n≥1:y+t a_n∈H_p, then ∀η∈(0,1) ∃compact E⊂[0,1] with m(E)>1−η and ∀x∈ℝ ∀s≠0 ∃n≥1:x+s a_n∉E.
hypotheses: The real sequence is fixed; nullness is unnecessary.
The finite positive C is independent of p,y,t,n.
H_p may depend on p and the sequence, but is uniform in y,t.
The normalized hitting condition holds pointwise with order ∀y∀t∃n.
conclusion: For each η∈(0,1), a compact E avoids all translates and signed nonzero dilates.
For B=max(1,C), p_k=η4^(−|k|)/(16B), the explicit construction gives m(E)≥1−7Cη/(24B)≥1−7η/24>1−η.
proof: Choose B=max(1,C), p_k=η4^(−|k|)/(16B), and corresponding H_k. All p_k belong to (0,1).
U is open, hence E is compact.
Signed normalization gives a point of every affine copy in U, hence outside E.
limitations: Conditional on existence of sparse normalized hitting sets; no such sets are constructed here.
Does not prove the general Erdős similarity conjecture or validate the hard hitting construction of the source manuscript.
No new Lean verification or native MRS import.

safe_extensions.name: measurable_hitting_sets
safe_extensions.statement: For measurable H_p, the same construction gives measurable avoiding F with m(F)≥1−7η/24. Inner regularity gives compact E⊂F with loss <η/2 and m(E)>1−19η/24>1−η.
